abstract: Attention-based rerankers score each candidate by the attention mass that retrieval heads route to it from the question, but the question, serving as a fixed query, carries limited information for locating relevant evidence. We propose Re3Rank, a listwise reranker built on reasoning-conditioned retrieval heads (RRHeads). A generator first writes a reasoning trace over the question and the candidates, and a scorer then uses the trace tokens as the attention query of a few selected RRHeads, reading relevance as continuous scores. We present a straight-through estimator to propagate the ranking loss through the discrete trace, so that the generator and the scorer can be trained jointly for ranking. Averaged over 9 benchmarks, Re3Rank outperforms 11 baseline rerankers: our 4B variant exceeds the strongest baseline by 3.11 NDCG@10 points on average, and even our 0.6B variant surpasses rerankers with up to 32B parameters.

sections.body: QRHead rerankers score each candidate by the attention mass that question tokens route to it. The paper argues that the question often lacks the information needed to locate relevant evidence. Re3Rank has a generator write a reasoning trace over the question and candidates. A scorer then uses the trace tokens as the attention query of a few selected RRHeads and reads relevance as continuous scores in one forward pass. The paper builds three variants on Qwen3 backbones at 0.6B, 4B, and 8B. These outperform 11 baseline rerankers on 9 benchmarks. The 4B variant exceeds QRRanker (4B) by 3.31 R@3 and 3.11 NDCG@10 on average.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: QRHead rerankers may be limited by question-only attention queries, so Re3Rank uses a generated reasoning trace as the query instead.

sections.body: The section defines a reranker as a function that maps the question and candidate set to one real-valued score per candidate. The objective is to maximize conditional Recall@k over the candidate pool. Gold binary relevance labels are used for training and evaluation and are not available to the reranker at inference. Rerankers are grouped into pointwise, pairwise, and listwise methods. Listwise methods gain cross-candidate reasoning at the cost of longer prefilled contexts. For QRHead rerankers, each candidate's score is the average, over a selected set of heads, of the attention mass routed from the question positions to that candidate.
sections.heading: Preliminaries
sections.headline: QRHead rerankers score each candidate by the attention mass the question routes to it, with no generated permutation.

sections.body: Re3Rank has a reasoning generator and a separate attention-based scorer, both initialized from the same backbone. The generator samples a reasoning trace, and the scorer uses the trace positions as the attention query of the selected RRHeads. Scores are normalized within each pool to the range set by a scale alpha of 8. The primary loss is a grouped contrastive cross-entropy. A Recall@k surrogate loss, weighted by lambda, is added to form the mixed ranking loss. Because sampling blocks gradients, a straight-through estimator relaxes the trace tokens in the backward pass. The authors state that this estimator is biased but gives a low-variance route into the generator. One backward pass updates both components.
sections.heading: Re3Rank
sections.headline: Re3Rank trains its generator and scorer jointly, passing the ranking loss through the discrete trace with a straight-through estimator.

sections.body: Head selection ranks all heads of each Qwen3 backbone by the attention mass that trace positions route to relevant candidates on a seed set of 800 labeled instances, and keeps the top two. Training uses 38,000 English questions from five source datasets, with up to 50 candidates per question retrieved by Qwen3-Embedding-8B. Evaluation covers nine test sets spanning Wikipedia multi-hop QA, open-domain factoid QA, long-narrative QA, and long-term conversational memory. All rerankers score the same top-50 pools. Baselines include QRRanker, Qwen3-Reranker, and ReasonRank. On the Macro-9 average, the 4B variant reaches 76.70 R@3 and 82.23 NDCG@10, which are 14.61 and 11.96 points above the first-stage ranking.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: On the nine-benchmark average, the 4B variant reaches 76.70 Recall@3 and 82.23 NDCG@10, exceeding QRRanker by 3.31 and 3.11 points.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the method. A generated trace serves as the attention query of a few selected RRHeads, and a straight-through estimator carries the ranking loss through the discrete trace so that the generator and scorer train jointly. On nine benchmarks, Re3Rank outperforms existing rerankers across model scales. Its smallest 0.6B variant already surpasses much larger baselines. The design also transfers across backbones. The authors suggest that its gains in downstream QA indicate potential as the retrieval component of agentic memory systems.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The 0.6B variant surpasses much larger baselines, and the design transfers across backbones, suggesting memory-system use.

sections.body: The generator is optimized only through the ranking loss, so its reasoning traces carry no guarantee of linguistic quality or readability to humans. All experiments rerank a fixed pool of the top 50 candidates returned by one first-stage retriever, Qwen3-Embedding-8B. The authors state that constraints on computational resources and experimental scale left open the correctness of the traces. Also left open are behavior with other retrievers and behavior with larger candidate pools, which may exceed the context window.
sections.heading: Limitations
sections.headline: Reasoning traces are optimized only for ranking, with no guarantee of readability, and all experiments used one retriever's top-50 pool.

sections.body: Appendix A details the head scan for Qwen3-4B. The seed set has 400 instances each from MuSiQue and NarrativeQA, with 2.31 relevant candidates per question on average. On this seed set, the first-stage order reaches 51.78 R@3 and 64.14 NDCG@10. Heads are ranked by gold mass, and the two highest, (23,10) and (21,8), form the RRHeads. Summing more heads does not reliably help. The top two reach 59.96 R@3 against 59.42 for (23,10) alone, a difference the paired bootstrap does not find significant. The top 16 heads fall 1.40 R@3 points below the top two. Appendix B gives full reranking tables for the nine benchmarks.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix covers Qwen3-4B RRHead selection and head-count and redundancy checks, plus full reranking tables.
